title: "Documentation and resources"

*Reading a library or a web service as a catalogue of contracts.*

::: {.callout-note}
## Draft stub — planned contents
The week-twelve lecture, grafted onto the classes material. Teaches reading the reference documentation of a library, or the documentation of a web API, as a list of functions and endpoints each with a contract: what it takes and what it returns, understood without reading how it works inside. Connects this to the class idea that an object is a thing with methods you call by their contract. Teaches directing the assistant to combine such capabilities, and catching it when it invents functions or parameters that are not there, for which the real documentation is the test. This is the skill that makes the finale possible, because it is how a student learns what is possible. Introduces the dataframe here as one such resource, pointing to the dataframes note, and keeps real data analysis out of scope.
:::
